protagonistIdentity.summary: The player creates the hero's name, body presentation, lineage, class, subclass, and palette. The story never treats a placeholder label as the hero's true name.
runtimeCopyRules: Use the saved character name when available.
Use Reliquary Bearer, bearer, hero, or protagonist when a neutral title is needed.
Never turn a planning placeholder into a character name or title.
Avoid fixed pronouns in authored canon until player pronoun support exists.

openingChapter.title: The Day the Bellroot Rang
openingChapter.summary: Veyrhold's buried oath-bells ring for the first time in a generation. The player-created hero is sent below as a witness, lamp-runner, and ledger-bearer before any blade is drawn.
openingChapter.openingPremise: The hero was raised on the edge of Veyrhold's Bellroot Commons, where civic records are grown into living root-brass and every oath is supposed to leave a clean mark. Their own record is damaged: not erased, not cursed, simply unfinished. When the lower bells wake and call for a living witness, the city chooses the one person whose name-thread the reliquary cannot file away.

firstLocation.name: The Bellroot Vestibule
firstLocation.visualSummary: A warm underground civic chamber below Veyrhold: bronze root-bells hang from living stone, amber oath-lamps line the floor, glass memory panes show half-restored city records, and the locked north road waits behind a black-stone gate.
setPieces: The Descent Ledger, a brass-root desk that records the player's chosen identity.
The Oath-Lamp Arcade, a curved row of dim lamps that teaches movement and inspection.
Ilo's Oracle Cradle, a blue-glass perch where the little oracle wakes and begins tracking the hero.
The Gate Monolith, a black-stone memory machine that explains why the reliquary opened.
The Quiet Forge Pedestal, a safe crafting altar that introduces upgrades after the intro.
The Warden's Antechamber, the first place where danger becomes combat.
sensoryDetails: Dust hangs in warm shafts of light like slow sparks.
The bells are huge, but their ringing is felt in the ribs before it is heard.
Glass memory panes blink with names, route maps, and debts too old to collect.
The floor hums politely when the hero walks where a witness is expected.
Every lamp that wakes throws a small gold reflection across the north gate.
firstLocation.openingSafetyRule: The first minutes are exploration, identity, and wonder. Combat begins only after the player understands the room, meets Ilo, studies the gate, and claims the first relic hook.

openingFlow.title: Sign the Descent Ledger
openingFlow.summary: The hero touches the brass-root ledger and the player confirms name, lineage, class, subclass, palette, and the first visible identity choices.

openingFlow.title: Relight the Oath-Lamps
openingFlow.summary: The player learns movement and inspection by waking three lamps that reveal murals of Veyrhold's first promise.

openingFlow.title: Wake Ilo
openingFlow.summary: A small oracle named Ilo wakes in a blue-glass cradle, jokes about counting the quiet, and becomes the player's guide without taking control away.

openingFlow.title: Study the Gate Monolith
openingFlow.summary: The monolith recognizes the hero as a living witness and reveals that the reliquary network is not dead; it is waiting for someone who can carry unfinished vows.

openingFlow.title: Claim the Loom-Shard Charm
openingFlow.summary: The first relic is not a weapon. It is a memory charm that lets old doors and future companions recognize the hero's chosen path.

openingFlow.title: Hear the Quiet Forge
openingFlow.summary: The forge explains that upgrades are oathwork: shard, pressure, heat, and a choice the item can remember.

openingFlow.title: Enter the Warden's Antechamber
openingFlow.summary: Only after the opening lessons does the room reveal broken sentries and the first safe combat trial.

keyCharacters.summary: A Veyrhold-raised hero whose civic name-thread was never fully restored. The missing record is not a destiny label; it is space for the player's identity and choices.

keyCharacters.name: Ilo
keyCharacters.summary: A palm-sized oracle with blue-glass wings, a brave mouth, and a habit of turning danger into useful instructions.

keyCharacters.name: Keeper Elian
keyCharacters.summary: The civic caretaker who opens the descent stairs. Elian believes the reliquary chose a witness, not a weapon.

keyCharacters.name: The First Reliquary
keyCharacters.summary: An old oath-machine that stores Veyrhold's earliest routes, names, promises, and repairs. It speaks through bells, lamps, and recorded fragments.

dialogueSamples.speaker: Keeper Elian
dialogueSamples.line: No blades unless the lower doors open. You are going below as a witness, not a soldier.

dialogueSamples.speaker: Ilo
dialogueSamples.line: I was counting the quiet. Then you arrived and ruined it. Good.

dialogueSamples.speaker: Gate Monolith
dialogueSamples.line: Name: player-kept. Oath: unbroken. Road: listening.

dialogueSamples.speaker: The First Reliquary
dialogueSamples.line: Veyrhold asked for a lock. The road asked for a person.

firstQuest.title: Light the Bellroot Below
firstQuest.summary: Enter the Bellroot Vestibule, restore the oath-lamps, meet Ilo, and learn why The First Reliquary opened before the first fight begins.
steps: Equip the charm when the chamber recognizes you.

codexEntries.title: The Bellroot Vestibule
codexEntries.summary: The civic threshold below Veyrhold where names, routes, lamps, and witness-oaths are recorded before a reliquary road opens.

codexEntries.title: Living Witness
codexEntries.summary: A person trusted by a reliquary to carry unfinished civic memory without being reduced to a stored record.

codexEntries.title: Ilo, Little Oracle
codexEntries.summary: A small companion oracle who marks danger, remembers choices, and speaks as if fear is just another puzzle with bad manners.
